question: Can an explicit map of policy revisions and their applicability reduce unnecessary refreshes without retaining stale or already-wrong claim decisions?
hypothesis: A model-produced change map plus claim-specific applicability routing can preserve unaffected decisions while identifying necessary updates more reliably than citation-text overlap or a gate without a change map.
unit: A fixed hypothetical applicant claim at two evidence snapshots. Only the named condition is judged; no whole eligibility, final selection, actual payment or legal conclusion.
design: The old cache is each model's actual first prediction, never the reference label. All strategies share the same cached old and fresh new predictions. Gates choose between them; invalid/uncertain gates or invalid caches trigger refresh. A map is inferred once per evidence bundle without claims or reference labels.
gate_target: Recheck when the revision changes, withdraws or leaves unresolved a rule relevant and applicable to the specified claim. A changed applicable threshold requires rechecking even when this profile's final truth value remains unchanged. Mere paraphrases and changes to other programs or conditions do not require rechecking.
metrics: errors retained from wrong old caches
actual model calls and observed request times
development: Authored revision controls and previously observed Jeju revision. Development outputs may guide one explicitly recorded refinement before new-document evaluation.
new_document_candidates: Seoul 2024 guarantee-fee support revised notice 2024-3494 and its original
Chungnam 2025 coal-power subcontractor welfare notice and December revision
prior_exposure: Search snippets of the candidate titles and Seoul change summary were seen before method design. Full new-source reading and annotations follow the method freeze. This is not external preregistration or blind human annotation.
robustness: Include genuine version changes, stable conditions, authored paraphrase and unrelated changes, partial missing evidence and prior-cache errors. Label authored counterfactuals separately from actual policy revisions.
cost: Fresh predictions are precomputed for evaluation and reused, so avoided refresh counts are counterfactual routing counts, not observed end-to-end latency savings. Gate and map overhead is included; API eval_count is not assumed to cover total generation.
publication: Publish code, authored probes, provisional annotations, source locators/hashes, selected output fields and plots. Keep complete official documents, extracted source text and raw source-derived model generations outside Git.
stopping_condition: Complete the frozen comparisons and declared follow-ups, recompute results, preserve all first outputs and earlier artifacts, then publish both repos and verify the live page. Failed hypotheses remain reportable outcomes.
